Paragraph: "They are fortunate, Lakshmana, for no cruel fate has torn them apart as it has torn me from my beloved..."
Situation/Problem_Faced: Comparing his cruel fate with the good fortune of undisturbed birds.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama reflects on his misfortune while recognizing the fortune of others.
Outcome/Resolution: He expresses his sense of tragic destiny.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Daiva (The mysterious workings of destiny/karma shaping human suffering)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Glimpses the heavy hand of destiny (Daiva) in human life, which tests even the most righteous souls.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Attributing tragedy to external fate while expressing sorrow over personal disruption.
